# Milestone brief — data-plane-governance-m1

**Title:** Boundary ADR owner-approved, committed, and binding in CLAUDE.md
**Kind:** milestone
**Roadmap:** data-plane-governance (plans/data-plane-governance/roadmap.yaml)
**Status:** planned
**Lane:** now
**Target:** 2026-07-11 -> 2026-07-15

## Parent epic

- data-plane-governance-e1 — Boundary ADR and binding CLAUDE.md constraints
  Draft, owner-approve, and commit the data-plane boundary ADR at .claude/docs/adr-data-plane-boundary.md — recording the three boundary rules (no agent dispatch or per-run agent memory in the server; writes only via offline ingest or operator-gated console actions; orchestrator loop moved to a separate repo or re-scoped as a client-side tool under tools/ with zero server-side state), the disposition of server/orchestrator/model_selector.py, and the candidate-layer principle for non-commercially-licensed external data — then land the boundary rules in CLAUDE.md as binding agent constraints. Vertical slice ends in committed, citable state that closes the orchestrator-loop placement question.

## Summary

The data-plane boundary ADR at .claude/docs/adr-data-plane-boundary.md is owner-approved and committed — closing the orchestrator-loop placement question — and CLAUDE.md carries the boundary rules as binding agent constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given the drafted ADR at .claude/docs/adr-data-plane-boundary.md, when the owner reviews it, then owner approval is recorded and the ADR is committed stating all three boundary rules (no agent dispatch or per-run agent memory in the server; writes only via offline ingest or operator-gated console actions; orchestrator loop moved to a separate repo or re-scoped as a client-side tool under tools/ with zero server-side state)
2. Given the committed ADR, when it is read, then it records a single choice for the orchestrator-loop placement, the disposition of server/orchestrator/model_selector.py, and the candidate-layer principle for non-commercially-licensed external data
3. Given the owner-approved ADR, when the CLAUDE.md amendment lands, then CLAUDE.md states the three boundary rules as binding agent constraints and the ADR records the chosen CLAUDE.md anchor (new hard-constraints section or extended section 4)

- (none)
